title: KV occupancy interference: synthetic multi-tenant sweep and regression detector
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a synthetic multi-tenant KV/prefix cache workload generator and CI-attached detector that measures occupancy-driven interference effects on tokens/sec and p95 latency across memory budgets. This ticket builds a reproducible sweep harness that varies tenant mix, object size distribution, prefix correlation, and memory constraints to map hit-rate vs latency vs memory curves and surface regressions automatically.
background: Recent incidents and internal benchmarks suggest that aggregate hit-rate masks tenant-level interference: a single noisy tenant can push eviction churn that increases p95 by >20% under moderate memory pressure. Existing fixtures focus on single-tenant hitrate sweeps; we need a targeted multi-tenant occupancy model plus automated regression checks to prevent regressions when changing eviction heuristics, prefetch, or batching logic.
approach: Design a workload DSL that composes N tenants with configurable: request rate, prefix correlation (zipf / synthetic clusters), object size distribution, and TTL/score distributions
Implement generator to emit traffic traces and live-replay harness that runs against local/integration kvcache binaries and dedicated bench infra
Measure per-tenant and aggregate metrics: tokens/sec, p95/p99 latency, eviction_rate, resident_memory_bytes, hit_rate, batch_utilization
Run parameter sweep over memory budgets (25%,50%,75% of working set), tenant skew (1:many heavy), and prefetch settings; produce heatmaps and Pareto frontiers
Add a regression detector that compares new runs against canonical baselines and raises alerts when p95 increases by >10% for any tenant at stable hit_rate or when tokens/sec drop >8%
Integrate detector into CI: nightly runs + gated checks for runtime-1.21 changes and PR label hook for performance review
acceptance_criteria: Harness can reproducibly run full sweep (3 memory budgets x 4 tenant mixes x 5 prefix correlations) within bench window and produce saved artifact JSON
Regression detector identifies injected regressions (we will simulate a +15% p95 increase) with >95% true-positive rate and <5% false-positive rate on baseline noise
Artifacts are uploaded to S3 with stable path and linked to dashboard; nightly CI job completes end-to-end and annotates PRs with performance badges
Visualizations exist: heatmap (hit-rate vs p95 vs memory), per-tenant latency CDFs, and Pareto front summary
